investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 141–149 seconds before the evals timed out. Because the pod never started, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints on the remote-agent pod spec. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable, preventing VM provisioning from starting and causing all three remote-agent eval checks to fail before any evidence can be collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so horizontal scaling to other nodes is not possible without changing the pod spec or adding node labels.

Tertiary — cluster has not scaled out to add new kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes: if autoscaling is configured, it may be disabled, misconfigured, or the scale-out event has not yet completed at the time of the eval run.

Lower confidence — a recent workload surge or leaked/stuck pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations even if total configured capacity is sufficient.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pods because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, no agent was created, and the remote-agent-runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected as Unschedulable, preemption was not possible (no lower-priority victims found), and the pods timed out after ~141–149 seconds without ever starting. investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pods because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, no agent was created, and the remote-agent-runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected as Unschedulable, preemption was not possible (no lower-priority victims found), and the pods timed out after ~141–149 seconds without ever starting. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is scoped to the observability eval infrastructure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
